title: Transmission Media, Transceivers and Topologies

header.html: 1.5 Compare and contrast transmission media and transceivers (wireless 802.11, cellular, satellite; wired 802.3, single-mode and multimode fiber, direct attach copper, coaxial, cable speeds, plenum; Ethernet and Fibre Channel transceivers, SFP and QSFP; connector types); 1.6 Compare and contrast network topologies, architectures and types (mesh, hybrid, star, spine and leaf, point to point, three-tier hierarchy, collapsed core, north-south and east-west traffic flows)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Wired and wireless media

Medium Facts
Twisted pair copper (802.3) Cat 5e: 1 Gbps to 100 m; Cat 6: 1 Gbps (10 Gbps to about 55 m); Cat 6a: 10 Gbps to 100 m; Cat 7 shielded; Cat 8: 25/40 Gbps to about 30 m. UTP unshielded, STP shielded (less interference) [Verify live]
Single-mode fiber (SMF) One light path, laser, long distances (kilometers)
Multimode fiber (MMF) Many light paths, LED or VCSEL, shorter distances (hundreds of meters), cheaper optics
Direct attach copper (DAC) / twinaxial Pre-terminated copper cable with transceivers built in, very short (a few meters), between racks or devices
Coaxial Cable TV and broadband; F-type connectors
Wireless 802.11 Wi-Fi (Module 10)
Cellular WAN access over mobile networks (4G/5G)
Satellite Remote areas, high latency

Plenum cable has fire-retardant, low-smoke jacket and must be used in air-handling spaces (above ceilings, in ducts); non-plenum (PVC) is cheaper and not for plenum spaces.

Exam tip

. Long distance = single-mode fiber. Short, cheap server links between racks = DAC. Cable in a ceiling air space = plenum rated.

2Transceivers and connectors

Item Facts
SFP (small form-factor pluggable) Hot-swappable module for 1 Gbps (SFP+ for 10 Gbps)
QSFP (quad SFP) Four lanes, 40 Gbps and higher (QSFP+, QSFP28)
Protocols Ethernet or Fibre Channel (FC) for storage; the transceiver must match the protocol, fiber type and speed

Connector Used with
RJ11 Telephone (2 pairs)
RJ45 Ethernet twisted pair
F-type Coaxial (cable TV, broadband)
BNC Coaxial, older networks and video
SC (subscriber connector) Fiber, square push-pull
LC (local connector) Fiber, small, most common on SFP
ST (straight tip) Fiber, round twist-lock
MPO (multi-fiber push on) Fiber, many fibers in one connector (QSFP)

3Topologies and architectures

Topology Description
Mesh Devices connect to many others; redundant, costly (full or partial mesh)
Star / hub and spoke Devices connect to a central point; single point of failure at the center
Hybrid A mix of topologies
Point to point A dedicated link between two sites
Spine and leaf Data center design: every leaf switch connects to every spine switch; predictable low latency, east-west traffic
Three-tier hierarchical Core (fast backbone), distribution (policy, routing between VLANs), access (end devices)
Collapsed core Core and distribution combined in one layer (smaller sites)
Traffic flow Direction
North-south Between clients outside and servers in the data center
East-west Between servers inside the data center

Exam tip

. Lots of server-to-server traffic = spine and leaf (east-west). Campus with core, distribution and access = three-tier. Smaller site = collapsed core.

Exam tip

. Match the transceiver, fiber type and speed at both ends; a single-mode optic does not work on multimode fiber.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A link must span 15 kilometers between two buildings. Which medium fits best?

  • ASingle-mode fiber
  • BMultimode fiber
  • CCat 6a twisted pair
  • DCoaxial cable
Show the answer

Answer: A. Single-mode fiber supports very long distances.

S2Which cable type must be installed above a drop ceiling used as an air-return space?

  • ANon-plenum PVC cable
  • BCoaxial patch cable
  • CDirect attach copper
  • DPlenum-rated cable
Show the answer

Answer: D. Plenum cable has a fire-retardant, low-smoke jacket for air-handling spaces.

S3A data center has heavy server-to-server traffic and needs predictable latency. Which design fits?

  • ASpine and leaf
  • BThree-tier hierarchical
  • CStar with one central switch
  • DHub and spoke
Show the answer

Answer: A. Spine and leaf is built for east-west traffic.

S4Which fiber connector is small, push-pull, and common on SFP modules?

  • ALC
  • BST
  • CSC
  • DBNC
Show the answer

Answer: A. LC is the small connector used on most SFPs.

S5Two switches in adjacent racks must be linked cheaply over 2 meters at 10 Gbps. What fits best?

  • ASingle-mode fiber with long-range optics
  • BCat 5e with RJ11 connectors
  • CA satellite link
  • DA direct attach copper cable
Show the answer

Answer: D. DAC is a short, inexpensive pre-terminated link.

S6Which layer of the three-tier model provides the high-speed backbone?

  • ADistribution
  • BAccess
  • CCollapsed
  • DCore
Show the answer

Answer: D. The core is the fast backbone.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Which Cat standard supports 10 Gbps to 100 meters?

Show the answer

Cat 6a.

R2What is the difference between SMF and MMF?

Show the answer

Single-mode uses one light path for long distance; multimode uses many paths for shorter distance.

R3What does SFP stand for?

Show the answer

Small form-factor pluggable.

R4Which connector is used for Ethernet twisted pair?

Show the answer

RJ45.

R5What is east-west traffic?

Show the answer

Traffic between servers inside the data center.

R6What is a collapsed core?

Show the answer

Core and distribution layers combined in one.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Copper Cat 5e/6 1 Gbps, Cat 6a 10 Gbps 100 m, Cat 8 short; STP vs UTP; plenum
Fiber SMF long distance (laser), MMF short; DAC for short links
Transceivers SFP (1 Gbps), QSFP (40 Gbps+); Ethernet vs Fibre Channel
Connectors RJ45, RJ11, F-type, BNC, SC, LC, ST, MPO
Topologies mesh, star, hybrid, point to point, spine and leaf, three-tier, collapsed core
